clue.text: Capital support for the traveller!

parts.note: the capital of a column is its head, its top part
a rest is something to lean on

explanation.surface: Money backing for someone setting out on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Support' does double duty: it gives the second half and is also part of the definition, which the exclamation mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: A headrest is the padded cushion on a car or aircraft seat that supports a passenger's head.

clue.text: Water only is given

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a lake or pond

explanation.surface: A prisoner's ration: only water is handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: A mere is a small lake, chiefly in English place names; as an adjective it means no more than.

clue.text: Curve for decoration in a motor

indicators.note: the honour is placed inside the vehicle word, sitting within it

parts.note: motor is British for a car
the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour

explanation.surface: A curved trim fitted as decoration inside a car.
explanation.walkthrough: CA(MBE)R.
explanation.definitionFit: Camber is the slight convex curve of a road surface or a beam.

clue.text: Disposal of cider and rum

indicators.note: rum is British slang for odd or strange, so the letters come out oddly arranged

parts.note: eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Getting rid of the bar's cider and rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' reads as a drink alongside cider, but it is the adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Riddance is the act of getting rid of something unwanted, as in 'good riddance'.

clue.text: Plant bearing fruit — showy, rather sour

parts.note: a vine is a climbing plant that bears grapes
garish means gaudy, too bright

explanation.surface: A fruiting plant looks flashy but its fruit tastes sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinegarish means somewhat like vinegar, sharp and acidic in taste or temper.

clue.text: A little cavern always most spectacular in spring

indicators.note: a little of something is just a part of it, here a run of letters inside the words

parts.note: the letters straddle the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: A small cave always looks its best in springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside ca(VERN AL)ways; the definition describes a thing that is at its showiest in spring, such as a vernal flower.
explanation.definitionFit: Vernal means belonging to or appearing in spring, from the Latin word for that season.

clue.text: Left always before time — such an advantage

parts.note: L is the standard abbreviation for left
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a lead always held over time gives a lasting edge.
explanation.definitionFit: Leverage is a position of power or influence that lets you gain more than your effort alone would.

clue.text: No huge pie, but it's adequate

indicators.note: in printing, pie is type that has been spilt and jumbled, so the letters are mixed up

parts.note: six letters taken as written

explanation.surface: The pie isn't large, but it will do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pie' reads as food; printers call scattered type pie, which makes it an anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Enough means sufficient, as much as is needed, which is what adequate means.

clue.text: One thousand are about to stay in the same place

indicators.note: to be about something is to surround it, so the first two pieces go round what follows

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
the Roman numeral for a thousand
to bide is to stay or wait, as in 'bide your time'

explanation.surface: A thousand people are about to stay put in one spot.
explanation.walkthrough: IBIDEM is the Latin term used in footnotes, usually shortened to ibid.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibidem is Latin for 'in the same place', used in references to cite the source just quoted.

clue.text: Some get paid less when not at work

indicators.note: 'some' asks for only part of the following words, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words

explanation.surface: Some workers are paid less when they are not working.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits inside pa(ID LE)ss.
explanation.definitionFit: Idle describes someone who is unemployed or inactive, with no job to do at present.

clue.text: Vegetable beds a baron made

definitions.note: singular, though the answer is plural

indicators.note: the letters are made, built up afresh, into a new arrangement

parts.note: ten letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A lord has had vegetable beds dug on his estate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beds' suggests a garden, which fits the vegetable but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Broad beans are a common garden vegetable, large flat beans grown in pods.

clue.text: Hempen coat?

parts.note: surface reading: a garment woven from hemp fibre
setter's reading: a word that is both a cannabis cigarette and a kind of short jacket

explanation.walkthrough: Hemp is cannabis, and a reefer is a joint; a reefer is also a short double-breasted jacket.
explanation.definitionFit: Reefer names both a thick sailor's jacket and a cannabis cigarette, so it is a coat with a hemp connection.

clue.text: People never repeat such a blunder!'

definitions.text: People never repeat such a blunder!'

parts.words: People never repeat such a blunder!'
parts.note: surface reading: a mistake so embarrassing that everyone learns from it
setter's reading: nobody can repeat it because the mistake killed them

explanation.walkthrough: The clue sounds like a lesson learnt; the dark joke is that the one who made it is no longer alive to try again.
explanation.definitionFit: A fatal error is a mistake that causes death or total failure, so it cannot be made twice.

clue.text: Soldier going around quarters with a friend in sociable fashion

indicators.note: something going around another thing encircles it, so one piece wraps the next

parts.note: GI is an American private soldier
east and north, two quarters of the compass
an ally is a friend or supporter

explanation.surface: A soldier makes the rounds of the barracks with a mate, being friendly.
explanation.walkthrough: Quarters means compass points, not lodgings: G(EN)I then ALLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Genially means in a warm, friendly and cheerful manner, the way a sociable person behaves.

clue.text: Painter finding a flighty little creature in a muddle

indicators.note: a muddle is a confused jumble, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: a tit is a small flitting songbird
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An artist discovers a small bird or insect has got itself into a tangle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a muddle' reads as one phrase, but 'in' and 'a' are letters for the mix and only 'muddle' signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was the great sixteenth-century Venetian painter of the Renaissance.

clue.text: Any crest used to show lineage

indicators.note: the letters are used as raw material and put to work in a new order

parts.note: eight letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A family coat of arms displayed to prove noble descent.
explanation.definitionFit: Ancestry is one's line of descent from forebears, the same as lineage.

clue.text: Combat is in the balance

indicators.note: one word sits within the other, placed inside it

parts.note: the rest is what remains, the balance left over
taken as written

explanation.surface: The outcome of the fight hangs in the balance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the balance' reads as an idiom for undecided; here balance means the remainder. RES(IS)T.
explanation.definitionFit: To combat something is to fight against or oppose it, which is what resisting does.

clue.text: Rent deposit indicating depression

definitions.note: a phrase describing the answer, which is a noun

parts.note: a rent is a rip in cloth
to drop something is to set it down

explanation.surface: A tenant's rent deposit is a sign the market is in a slump.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent and deposit look like housing money; they are a rip and a setting down.
explanation.definitionFit: A teardrop is a single tear, a visible sign of sadness or low spirits.

clue.text: Fit to be a member of the boat-crew

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a sudden seizure or attack
second meaning: the oarsman nearest the stern who sets the pace

explanation.surface: Someone is fit enough to join the rowing eight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fit' reads as healthy, but it is a noun meaning an attack of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: A stroke is a sudden attack such as apoplexy; in rowing the stroke is the oarsman who sets the rhythm.

clue.text: Bad spirit permissible — it's taken for granted

definitions.note: a clause describing the answer, which is an adjective

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
licit means lawful or allowed

explanation.surface: A wicked mood is excused as acceptable and simply assumed.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is understood or assumed without being stated outright.

clue.text: Old forecaster old coppers tied up

parts.note: Old Moore's Almanack is a long-running British book of predictions
d was the abbreviation for pre-decimal British pennies, copper coins

explanation.surface: An elderly weatherman is held prisoner by former policemen.
explanation.walkthrough: Coppers suggests police, but here means pennies; d stood for old pence before 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: A boat that is moored is tied up to a quay or buoy.

clue.text: Get warm again here perhaps, returning thanks

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word after it is read backwards
'perhaps' says the word before is one possible arrangement of the letters, not the final one

parts.note: the four letters of this word rearranged
ta is informal British for thanks

explanation.surface: A cold person grateful to be warming up again by the fire.
explanation.walkthrough: The scan split 'returning' into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: To reheat is to warm something up once more after it has cooled.

clue.text: Less prudent when there's tasty food

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a thin slice of bacon

explanation.surface: People grow careless when delicious food is on offer.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasher is the comparative of rash, more reckless; a rasher is also a slice of bacon or ham.

clue.text: The correct footwear when in wig and gown?

definitions.text: The correct footwear when in wig and gown?

parts.words: The correct footwear when in wig and gown?
parts.note: surface reading: what a barrister should wear on their feet with their robes
setter's reading: wig and gown are worn in the law courts, so the shoes are named after that place

explanation.walkthrough: Barristers in British courts wear a wig and gown; the answer is a plain women's shoe whose name fits the setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Court shoes are low-cut plain women's shoes without fastenings, called pumps in America.

clue.text: Put in order that's quite considerable

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a verb, to make neat
second meaning: an adjective, as in a sizeable sum of money

explanation.surface: Arranging things properly can take a large amount of effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Tidy as a verb is to arrange neatly; informally a 'tidy sum' is a fairly large amount.

clue.text: The solicitor wants everything in French

definitions.meaning: first meaning: one who ..., pestering people for custom
second meaning: the French word for all

explanation.surface: The lawyer demands the lot, in French.
explanation.walkthrough: Solicitor reads as a lawyer, but here it is someone who solicits business.
explanation.definitionFit: A tout is a person who aggressively seeks customers; in French, tout means all or everything.

clue.text: Going round setting hundreds on the wrong route

indicators.note: a wrong version is an incorrect one, so these letters come out in the wrong order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral 500, that is five hundreds
the five letters reordered

explanation.surface: A traveller goes round in circles after being sent the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: D for 'hundreds' is loose: it is the numeral for five hundred, set in front of the mixed route.
explanation.definitionFit: A detour is a way of going round an obstacle instead of straight through, a roundabout route.

clue.text: He's responsible for producing effects

parts.note: surface reading: a special-effects technician on a film set
setter's reading: effects are a dead person's belongings, which someone named in the will must handle

explanation.walkthrough: Effects suggests film or stage, but here it means personal property left at death.
explanation.definitionFit: An executor is the person named in a will to carry out its terms and distribute the deceased's property.
